extracted.intended_audience: readers of Popular Science Monthly / general educated public interested in anthropology
extracted.subtask_description: Describing the observable characters and statistical/qualitative criteria used to identify, typify, and compare human races (physical features, coloration, hair/eye traits, adaptation, temperament, and effects of mixture). Intended as popular-scientific guidance on what features anthropologists record and how they reason about race-types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shape of skull and cranial proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Skull narrowness or broadness is a distinguishing feature of race (examples: narrow African skull contrasted with broader Tartar and North American faces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside facial form to typify races; illustrated comparisons (figures) show skull shape differences; skull breadth noted to vary with migration and intermarriage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shape of softer facial parts (nose, lips, cheeks, chin) as race-marks
rubrics_metrics.description: The shape of the softer parts — nose, lips, cheeks, chin, etc. — are often excellent marks to distinguish race.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: aquiline Persian nose vs snub negro nose; pushing up one's nose can imitate other races' nostril opening; portraits used to show such contrasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skin color / complexion as an important mark of race
rubrics_metrics.description: The color of the skin is described as an important mark of race, varying gradually from fairest to darkest without hard lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that darkest hue of negro is deep brown (not black); newborns change tint after birth; darkest tint not uniform over whole body (soles/palms); uses Broca's pattern-colors for recording tints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range and gradation of complexion (no hard boundaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct tints vary gradually from one to another rather than showing hard and fast lines between races.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides geographic continuum (fair whites → dark whites → Malays → American tribes → Australians → negroes) and warns earlier descriptions were careless; advocates Broca's color scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Broca's set of pattern-colors for recording skin and eye color
rubrics_metrics.description: Travelers record the color of any tribe with Broca's set of pattern-colors to achieve accuracy like a mercer matching silk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a modern corrective to previous careless race-tint descriptions; applies to skin and eye color recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaporation smell of the skin as a race-character
rubrics_metrics.description: The smell accompanying evaporation from the human skin differs in different races and indicates differences in skin secretions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested connection with liability to certain fevers; regarded as a race-character of some importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iris (eye) color and its complex patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Iris shows the greatest variety of color among humans; shades arranged (per Broca) as orange, green, blue, violet-gray, but often blend into a single hue at a distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that 'black' eyes are usually deep brown or violet, and darkest eyes prevail among darker-skinned peoples; light iris tints accompany fair complexions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hair color, form, and quantity as race markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Color (black most usual, flaxen/chestnut among fair-northern peoples), form (woolly/frizzy vs straight vs wavy/curly), and quantity vary by race and help distinguish groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes correlation between fair skin and fair hair, dark skin and dark hair, but warns rules for intermediates are impossible; examples: woolly African, straight Asiatic/American, flowing/wavy European.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopic hair cross-section morphology
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-sections of single hairs show differences (circular Mongolian hair, oval/elliptical European, flattened African, ribbon-like Papuan) relating to hair form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Pruner-Bey's sections and links microscopic form to macroscopic hair appearance (straight vs curly vs woolly vs frizzy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fitness/adaptation to climate and disease susceptibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Some races are constitutionally more fit or unfit for particular climates; races differ in susceptibility to specific diseases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Europeans more affected by yellow fever in equatorial regions while negroes/mulattoes less affected; measles less serious among Europeans but devastating among Fijians; adaptation to new climates required for flourishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperament and inbred temperament as race-characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Travelers notice distinctions in the temper of races suggesting inborn temperament and capacities of mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives comparisons (native Indian vs African negro in Brazil; melancholy Russian peasant vs vivacious Italian) and links temperament to historical patterns of civilization and decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual/moral capacities and educational responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences in intellectual and moral powers are inferred historically; a practical test cited is how well children of 'lower races' take a civilized education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims these children often learn as well up to about twelve years old then fall off relative to ruling-race children — cited as evidence in assessing mental capacities (note: presented as an asserted test in the article).

rubrics_metrics.name: Race as a statistical type centered on a representative mean (Quetelet method)
rubrics_metrics.description: A race comprises a regular set of variations centering around one representative type (mean stature, etc.), illustrated by Quetelet's binomial curve showing the typical man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains measuring a population (heights ordered) yields a central cluster (mean/typical) with fewer extremes; useful for estimating typical characteristics of a people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility of single portraits for uniform (uncivilized) tribes vs difficulty for mixed populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Single portraits can well represent uniform, intermarried tribes but are less useful for very mixed populations (e.g., English crowd).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises starting analysis with simple uniform races to understand variation before tackling complex mixed populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanence of race-type over long periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Race-characters can remain recognizable over many centuries (Egyptian monuments show permanence), though migration and crossing can modify types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ancient Egyptian monuments correspond to modern fellahs; race may remain for 30 centuries or a hundred generations unless altered by mixture or changed conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of intermarriage / crossing (intermediate characters, tendency to revert)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crossing between races produces intermediate characters (mulatto, quadroon, sambo) often intermediate in complexion/features, with variable tendency to revert to one parent type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives examples: mulatto traits intermediate; children may show European or Malay cast variably; hair texture often intermediate; Cafusas in Brazil show mixed hair traits; crossing explains innumerable intermediate varieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes of race change: intermarriage and altered conditions of life
rubrics_metrics.description: Marked changes in a nation's appearance must be sought in intermarriage with foreigners or altered conditions of life, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains migration and mixing as primary drivers of change; these factors account for diversity and local modifications of race-types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic/climatic distribution as explanatory factor for color and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Correlation between race color/type and climate is suggested (e.g., darkest races principally in tropical climates near equator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps of world distribution invoked; examples include black races along equatorial regions from West Africa to New Guinea, Melanesian gradation reflecting crossing, and role of climate in modifying types.
